question: On production SPAs with non-deterministic rendering (React/Vue virtual DOM, auth-dependent content, external data), do DOM structural features encode predictive state variation that persists even with K>=3 sufficient action history? Specifically: (1) does conditional PMI I(S_next; DOM | URL, ActionHistory_K=3) exceed zero with Bonferroni-corrected permutation p < 0.0167? (2) does a richer DOM representation (accessibility tree, computed styles, or multi-feature hash) capture variation invisible to visible_text_hash?
hypothesis: On production SPAs with non-deterministic rendering, the same action sequence can lead to different DOM states depending on external factors (user data, API responses, timing). Therefore, DOM structural features will exhibit conditional PMI > 0 even at K=3, because action-history memory alone is insufficient to predict the next DOM state when rendering is non-deterministic. This is materially different from the deterministic SPA setting where K=3 action history fully predicts next state (PMI=0.0 on all 3 sites, parent EXP-PHYSICS-34724244876).
falsifier: The claim is falsified if ANY of: (1) conditional PMI I(S_next; DOM | URL, ActionHistory_K=3) <= 0.0 with Bonferroni-corrected permutation p >= 0.0167 on ALL tested production SPAs AND ALL DOM representations; OR (2) positive control fails (random-label PMI significantly > 0 after correction); OR (3) null control fails (shuffled-label PMI significantly > 0 after correction); OR (4) data quality fails (< 300 valid transitions per SPA after filtering).
baselines: Action-history-only prediction P(S_next | ActionHistory_K) for K=1,2,3 — the strong beyond-memory null from parent. If action-history alone achieves high accuracy at K=3, DOM cannot add predictive value.
Nearest-neighbor retrieval on action-history sequence — baseline from WP-002B that matched rule performance on deterministic SPAs.
Frequency baseline P(S_next) — marginal next-state distribution, weak baseline.
URL-only baseline — structural zero on single-path SPAs, included for completeness.
positive_control: Random DOM labels: generate labels as SHA-256(counter) where counter is an integer independent of FSM state and action history. Conditional PMI I(S_next; random_label | URL, ActionHistory_K=3) should be approximately 0.0 (within noise). This fixes the parent experiment's positive control failure (synthetic SPA had deterministic FSM-coupled labels, PMI=1.69 bits vs expected 0.0). The random-label control tests the pipeline's ability to detect independence, which was untested in the parent.
null_control: Shuffled DOM labels: permute DOM labels within action-history strata (preserving the marginal distribution of DOM labels and action-history). Conditional PMI should be approximately 0.0. This is the same null control that passed in the parent (mean shuffled PMI=0.0 on dashboard K=1). Additionally, test shuffle within URL strata to account for multi-page SPAs.
measurement_validity: Each production SPA must yield >= 300 valid transitions after filtering (timeouts, crashes, auth redirects excluded). Multiple visits to the same page with different sessions/timing to elicit non-deterministic rendering.

DOM representations tested: (a) visible_text_hash (SHA-256 of visible text content), (b) accessibility_tree_hash (SHA-256 of accessibility tree structure), (c) numeric_structural (element_count, tree_depth, interactive_density, form_count), (d) multi_feature_hash (combined hash of text + structure + styles).
Action history lengths K=1,2,3 tested for all representations. K=3 is the discriminating test (parent established K=3 sufficient on deterministic SPAs).

Permutation test: 1000 permutations per (site, representation, K) stratum, shuffling DOM labels within action-history strata. Bonferroni correction across all tested combinations (n_sites * n_representations * n_K_values).
No target leakage: action history constructed from trajectory step ordering with <START> padding; no future information enters PMI computation.

Determinism check: compute P(S_next | S_current, Action) accuracy. On production SPAs with non-deterministic rendering, this should be < 1.0 (confirming non-determinism). If accuracy = 1.0, the SPA is deterministic and the result is interpretable under the parent's setting, not the production setting.
Data provenance: record site URL, crawl timestamps, action sequences, DOM snapshots with SHA-256 hashes, browser version, and network conditions.
decision_rule: If ALL of: (1) conditional PMI I(S_next; DOM | URL, ActionHistory_K=3) > 0.0 with Bonferroni-corrected permutation p < 0.0167 on >= 2/3 tested production SPAs (at least one DOM representation); (2) positive control passes (random-label PMI within 3 standard deviations of 0.0); (3) null control passes (shuffled-label PMI within 3 standard deviations of 0.0); (4) determinism check confirms non-deterministic rendering (accuracy < 1.0) on surviving SPAs; (5) >= 300 valid transitions per surviving SPA — verdict = SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST for C-WEB-DYNAMICS. If conditional PMI <= 0.0 or non-significant on ALL SPAs/representations — verdict = FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING. If controls fail or data quality insufficient — verdict = MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
product_consequence_positive: DOM integration into SPIDER's observation layer is warranted for production SPAs. Non-deterministic rendering creates genuine environmental dynamics where DOM encodes predictive state variation beyond action-history memory. SPIDER should capture and transmit DOM structural features as part of its observation substrate, enabling downstream agents to leverage environmental state signals that action sequences alone cannot provide.
product_consequence_negative: If DOM features have no conditional PMI beyond action-history memory on production SPAs, the DOM integration path for C-WEB-DYNAMICS is closed. SPIDER should focus on action-history-based state tracking and other non-DOM representations (network responses, API payloads, visual structure). The deterministic SPA finding generalizes: DOM hash-based state labeling is not predictive dynamics.
estimated_cost: Medium: requires crawling production SPAs (browser automation, network I/O, DOM parsing), multiple sessions per site to elicit non-deterministic rendering, and PMI computation across 4 representations x 3 K-values x n_sites. Estimated 2-4 hours of browser time + 1 hour analysis. No model calls required for analysis.
expected_information_gain: High: resolves the last open setting where DOM could encode predictive dynamics beyond memory (production SPAs with non-deterministic rendering). A positive result justifies DOM integration as a physics-informed observation layer. A negative result closes the DOM-hash representation path for C-WEB-DYNAMICS across all tested settings. Both outcomes materially change the product architecture decision.
